In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of converting an $\omega$ automaton with arbitrary acceptance conditions into a deterministic parity automaton (DPW) and the problem of converting a deterministic automaton with arbitrary Rabin or Street acceptance conditions into a DPW.
the problem of determinizing $\omega$-languages, and in particular, the construction of deterministic automata with as few states as possible.

a uniform construction of deterministic parity automata from $\omega$-regular languages with general acceptance conditions, and the corresponding bounds on the number or states and parity indices of the resulting automaton.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of states in a DPW is at most $2^{\mathit{min}(O(n^2 log n), n!)}$ and the number of parity indices is at most $O(\mathit{max}(n^2, \mathit{min}_{\omega}(k))$.
, for any $\omega$ language, there exists a DPW with O(n^2) states and $O(\sqrt{n^2})$ parity indices, where n is the number of states of the minimal automaton recognizing the language.
our construction is a significant improvement over the existing techniques for determinizing $\omega$-regular languages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our construction is the first one to determinize arbitrary $\omega$- automata with a polynomial number of acceptance conditions to a DPW.

the problem of determinizing a non-determinstic automaton with $k$ acceptance sets can be done with a number of states that is polynomial in $k$ (and $n$, the number of states in the input automaton).

we have unified the determinization of all types of $\omega$ automata, and have obtained a tight upper bound on the size of the resulting deterministic parity automaton for all types of $\Omega{(2^k)}$ acceptance pairs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of states in a deterministic automaton accepting a given $\omega$-regular language is at most exponential in the Rabin index of the language.
the determinization problem for $\omega$-languages can be solved in a unified fashion, irrespective of the acceptance condition.
the determinization of $\omega-$automata is a uniform problem.
